title: ASCEP Layer 3 — Serving configuration
description: Layer 3 of the five ASCEP layers. Declares framework, parallelism, batching and KV configuration. Topology binding (C3): every KV and throughput figure produced under this declaration is valid only at this tensor_parallel / pipeline_parallel / gpu_count triple.

framework.description: Serving framework name (e.g. vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, or other). No default assumed.

framework_version.description: Exact framework version string. 'latest' is non-conforming (C8).

container_digest.description: Immutable container image digest (sha256). Required by the reproduction bundle (C8). Null is acceptable on a device that runs no container, but chapter 3's R11 then asks the report to pin its code some other way, in framework_version or runtime_build. A declaration that pins none of the three cannot be reproduced by anyone, including its own author on another bench day, and is held to partial for that reason.

tensor_parallel.description: Tensor-parallel width. Per-GPU KV is NOT constant across widths (ascep.capacity.kv_heads_per_rank replicates heads once TP > n_kv_heads); all figures in the run layer MUST inherit this value (C3).

gpu_count.description: Devices in one replica = tensor_parallel * pipeline_parallel unless otherwise stated. Binds capacity figures (C3).

max_model_len.description: Framework maximum sequence length in tokens. A run above native_max_context_tokens without declaration invalidates context-bound throughput claims (C4). On a slotted runtime this is not the window that bounds one user's KV -- context_tokens_per_slot is, because the configured context is divided among the slots -- and sizing KV from the configured figure instead over-promises by exactly the slot count.

max_model_len_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when max_model_len is null (C1).

memory_utilization.description: Framework's own memory cap (vLLM gpu_memory_utilization, SGLang mem_fraction_static, or equivalent), dimensionless in (0,1]. REQUIRED and never nullable: it is the most frequently omitted number in published benchmarks, and without it a KV measurement cannot be reproduced and analytic projections disagree with it by multiples. Input to ascep.capacity.kv_pool_bytes and calibration target of calibrate_memory_utilization.

batching_mode.description: Batching discipline. Static batching invalidates comparison against continuous-batching runs at the same concurrency. This describes the scheduler inside a server-batched runtime; a runtime that admits one request at a time has no scheduler to describe, which is why runtime_class 'serial' requires this to be null. A serial report wearing a batching label validates clean and then reads as a claim about concurrency the machine cannot make.

max_num_seqs.description: Scheduler cap on concurrent sequences, if set. Units: sequences.

max_num_seqs_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when max_num_seqs is null (C1).

max_num_batched_tokens.description: Scheduler cap on batched tokens per step, if set. Units: tokens.

max_num_batched_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when max_num_batched_tokens is null (C1).

prefix_caching.description: Prefix cache state. An untracked prefix-cache hit inflates measured throughput and is a required explanation for any roofline_efficiency at or above 1.0.

kv_cache_offload.description: Whether KV is offloaded to host memory. If on, calibrate_memory_utilization may return an effective utilization above 1.0 — that is a flag, not a result.

kv_cache_quantized.description: Whether runtime KV quantization applies beyond model kv_precision. This records that a quantization happened, not what it left: the element sizes live in kv_cache_type_k and kv_cache_type_v. The KV floor needs bytes per element, so 'on' quoted without those two leaves the floor uncomputable while looking like a complete declaration.

speculative_decoding.description: Speculative decoding state; MUST be off for protocol-comparable ITL claims unless the draft configuration is fully declared.

engine_reported_kv_cache_tokens.description: KV cache size in tokens as reported by the engine at startup (M). THE number to trust: the protocol REQUIRES preferring it over the analytic memory model, and calibrate_memory_utilization SHOULD be used to reconcile before projecting to other context lengths. Units: tokens.

engine_reported_kv_cache_tokens_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when engine_reported_kv_cache_tokens is null (C1). Without it, every KV-floor figure in the report is (I) at best.

cold_start_to_ready_s.description: Measured seconds from process start to ready-to-serve (M). Units: seconds.

cold_start_to_ready_s_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when cold_start_to_ready_s is null (C1).

framework_version_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when framework_version is null (C1).

container_digest_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when container_digest is null (C1).

memory_utilization_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when memory_utilization is null (C1).

batching_mode_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when batching_mode is null (C1).

prefix_caching_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when prefix_caching is null (C1).

kv_cache_offload_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when kv_cache_offload is null (C1).

kv_cache_quantized_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when kv_cache_quantized is null (C1).

chunked_prefill_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when chunked_prefill is null (C1).

speculative_decoding_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when speculative_decoding is null (C1).

media_preprocessing.description: Deployment-level media preprocessing: sampling rate, frame cap and pixel budget are fixed at server start and shared by every client of the endpoint, exactly like max_model_len, because the engine measured for this protocol refuses per-request media overrides (addendum A1). OPTIONAL at this level because a text-only deployment has no media preprocessing to declare; the obligation for a multimodal deployment to declare it is enforced in the report schema, not in this file.

video_sampling_fps.description: Frames sampled per second of source video, fixed at server start. This is the delivered rate; the workload layer declares the requested rate, and a report where the two disagree without a note describes a workload the server did not run.

video_sampling_fps_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when video_sampling_fps is null (C1).

video_max_frames.description: Hard cap on sampled frames per request, fixed at server start. Null means unbounded, which means the context length is unbounded -- a claim about the deployment, so it still takes a (U) reason saying the cap was checked and found absent rather than never looked for.

video_max_frames_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when video_max_frames is null (C1).

image_pixel_budget_px.description: Total pixel budget of the preprocessor per image or per sampled frame set, fixed at server start: a count of pixels (width times height per image, or the summed frame budget after sampling), never an edge length. A realistic value has the shape of 16777216 (4096 x 4096); a reader who mistakes the quantity for a longest-edge limit writes 4096, which as a pixel budget is a 64 x 64 image, roughly 4,096 times too small. This is the setting that binds silently: when measured prompt tokens stop responding to input size, the number being measured is this cap, not the workload, and a capacity model fed that column sizes the cluster for a workload nobody can run. Required whenever the served model accepts image or video; null only with a (U) reason.

image_pixel_budget_px_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when image_pixel_budget_px is null (C1).

mm_processor_cache_gb.description: Size of the engine's cache of processed media tensors, in GiB. A benchmark replaying identical media hits this cache and reports a speedup the production workload will never see, and nothing in the response reveals it.

mm_processor_cache_gb_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when mm_processor_cache_gb is null (C1).

per_request_override_supported.description: Whether the engine honours per-request media-processing overrides at all. The default assumption is false: the engine measured for this protocol answers per-request mm_processor_kwargs with HTTP 400, so declaring true while clients send per-request settings publishes a workload the server did not run.

notes.description: Free-form prose keyed by field name, recording why a declared non-null value is what it is: that mm_processor_cache_gb is 0 on purpose, so every request pays host-side decode and patchify rather than hiding preprocessing behind a cache. Complements the (U) mechanism, which can only justify a null. A note NEVER substitutes for a value, never satisfies C1 beside a null, and is not evidence: it changes no tier and no conformance grade.

image_input_transport.description: How image bytes reach the server. Base64 inflates a request body by about 4/3, so a 1 MB JPEG becomes roughly 1.37 MB of JSON per request; at high concurrency that saturates the client and the report blames the server.

image_input_transport_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when image_input_transport is null (C1).

runtime_class.description: The structural fact about admitted concurrency. 'server-batched': the engine schedules many sequences in one forward pass (vLLM, SGLang, TGI). 'slotted': a fixed number of independent slots, each with its own context (llama-server --parallel, LM Studio). 'serial': one request at a time; a second either queues or is refused (llama-cli, mlx_lm.generate, a default Ollama install). Not a synonym for batching_mode: batching_mode describes the scheduler inside a server-batched runtime, and on a runtime that admits one request there is no scheduler to describe. Takes no null for the same reason memory_architecture does not: it is the discriminator every conditional in this schema keys off, and a null discriminator leaves the document in no branch at all. Every reporter knows whether their server accepts a second request while the first is generating.

parallel_slots.description: How many requests the runtime admits concurrently before queueing; the number ASCEP's throughput floor is allowed to multiply by. On a serial runtime it MUST be 1: the aggregate tok/s measured at concurrency 1 is the only aggregate tok/s there is, so a floor that multiplies by anything larger produces a user count the machine physically cannot honour, and the report looks conforming. On a slotted runtime it MUST be a non-null integer. On 'server-batched' it may be null because max_num_seqs already carries it. Null only with parallel_slots_u_reason set. Units: requests. Not required of a server-batched runtime, where max_num_seqs is the same ceiling; where both are declared they must agree, because a throughput floor multiplied by the larger of two disagreeing ceilings is the over-promising direction.

parallel_slots_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when parallel_slots is null (C1).

context_tokens_per_slot.description: The per-session window after the configured context is divided among slots. On a slotted runtime this, not max_model_len, is what bounds one user's KV: llama-server -c 32768 --parallel 4 gives each slot 8192 tokens, and quoting the undivided window over-promises by exactly the slot count. The KV floor MUST be computed from this value. Null only on non-slotted runtimes or if unknown, with context_tokens_per_slot_u_reason set. Units: tokens.

context_tokens_per_slot_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when context_tokens_per_slot is null (C1).

context_overflow_policy.description: What the runtime does when a request exceeds its window: 'refuse', 'truncate', or 'shift' (llama.cpp's context shift silently evicts the oldest tokens and continues). 'refuse' is the only value that leaves the measurement honest. Under 'truncate' or 'shift', a sweep whose prompts outgrow the window is measuring a shorter workload than the one declared and reporting throughput that is high for exactly that reason, so a non-'refuse' value MUST accompany a statement of the longest prompt in the sweep. Null only if unknown, with context_overflow_policy_u_reason set.

context_overflow_policy_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when context_overflow_policy is null (C1).

kv_cache_type_k.description: Element type of the K cache (e.g. 'f16', 'q8_0', 'q4_0', 'fp8'). The KV floor needs bytes per element; kv_cache_quantized: 'on' says a quantisation happened without saying how many bytes it left, so the floor cannot be computed from it. Required non-null whenever kv_cache_quantized is 'on'. K and V are separate fields because llama.cpp quantises them separately (-ctk / -ctv) and asymmetric settings are common. The literal 'n-a' means the runtime applies no per-tensor override and the model declaration's kv_precision governs both caches; null means the element type is genuinely unknown and needs its (U) justification. The distinction matters because only one of those two states leaves the KV floor computable.

kv_cache_type_k_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when kv_cache_type_k is null (C1).

kv_cache_type_v.description: Element type of the V cache (e.g. 'f16', 'q8_0', 'q4_0', 'fp8'). The KV floor needs bytes per element; kv_cache_quantized: 'on' says a quantisation happened without saying how many bytes it left, so the floor cannot be computed from it. Required non-null whenever kv_cache_quantized is 'on'. Declared separately from kv_cache_type_k because llama.cpp quantises the two caches independently and asymmetric settings are common. The literal 'n-a' means the runtime applies no per-tensor override and the model declaration's kv_precision governs both caches; null means the element type is genuinely unknown and needs its (U) justification. The distinction matters because only one of those two states leaves the KV floor computable.

kv_cache_type_v_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when kv_cache_type_v is null (C1).

weights_residency.description: Whether the weights are pinned in memory ('resident') or mapped from disk and evictable ('mmap-paged'). The weights floor assumes resident. On a unified machine under memory pressure an mmap-paged model pages to NVMe mid-decode, and the resulting throughput is a measurement of the SSD. Declaring 'mmap-paged' marks the weights floor as a soft bound rather than a hard one.

weights_residency_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when weights_residency is null (C1).

runtime_build.description: Build identifier where the version string does not identify the code: llama.cpp's 'b4589 (f7f1d9a)' is the identity; 'llama.cpp' plus a date is not. Chapter 3's R11 asks a report to pin its serving code by at least one of container_digest, a framework_version naming a released build, or this field. That is a grading rule rather than a validator rule on purpose: a report may honestly pin none of the three and declare itself partial, and making the validator refuse it would teach reporters to invent a build string instead of admitting the gap.

runtime_build_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when runtime_build is null (C1).

model_artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the weights file the server actually loaded (64 lowercase hex characters). Quantisation names are not identities: two files both called 'Q4_K_M' from two requantisers differ in which tensors were left at higher precision, and therefore in both quality and size. The digest is the only thing that makes a local run reproducible. Never conditionally required: hashing a 40 GB file is a real cost, and a null declines with a (U) reason while the run stays auditable through runtime_build and container_digest.

model_artifact_sha256_u_reason.description: (U) justification required when model_artifact_sha256 is null (C1).

notes.description: Free-form prose keyed by field name, recording why a declared non-null value is what it is: that prefix_caching is on because production runs it on, not because it flattered the measurement. Keys MUST be field names this schema declares -- a note is an annotation on a declaration, not a place to record something the schema has no field for, and an invented key puts a fact where no reader queries it and no checker sees it. Complements the (U) mechanism, which can only justify a null. A note NEVER substitutes for a value, never satisfies C1 beside a null, and is not evidence: it changes no tier and no conformance grade.
